title: Daily Meditation Practice Method
content: Three deep-breathing pauses each day: Find a quiet place, stand or sit, and close your eyes. First deep breath: as you inhale, imagine bringing the air to your abdomen; as you exhale, release slowly and feel your body relax. Pause for a moment. Second deep breath: as you inhale, feel your chest expand; as you exhale, release tension. Pause again. Third deep breath: as you inhale, feel fullness from the top of your head to your toes; as you exhale, bring your attention back to the present. Repeat every day to build the habit.

First infusion: a floral aroma fills the nose; the liquor is bright golden and translucent; the first sip is slightly astringent but quickly melts away, leaving a long sweet aftertaste. Third infusion: an aged aroma faintly appears, the liquor is orange-red, the mouthfeel is full, and the throat feel is deep. Compared with the ripe Pu’er I usually drink, the raw Pu’er has a brighter, more elevated aroma and richer layers of flavor, but lacks the mellow, glutinous smoothness of ripe Pu’er. The infused leaves are plump and tender, with good activity.

content: Completed the first draft of “The Depth of Green,” about 1,200 words, in a flow state.

title: Record of sisters' discussion on cultural and creative products
content: My sister looked at my cultural-creative design proofs and suggested turning the Green Lake illustrations into a series, and shooting creative short videos to run on Xiaohongshu. She said my paintings have spirit, but need story packaging. While she took a half-hour nap, I drew a mind map centered on the Green Lake series, Xiaohongshu operation strategy, and story packaging.

title: Sisters' Old Town Walk and Bookstore Shopping Record
content: Today I walked with my elder sister Yutong from Nanping Pedestrian Street to Mingyuan Bookstore on Wenlin Street. We bought freshly baked flower cakes and fried mushrooms with chili powder, chatting about childhood summers as we walked. At the bookstore, I chose a collection of essays by a local Yunnan writer and chatted with Uncle Qin about my sister's funny habit of reading comics for free when she was little, as well as my thoughts on Lin Shen's new work. Full of memories and rewards.

title: Parents' oral history
content: Father: After returning to the city, he reviewed his studies here and looked forward to the future; Mother: When she got married, the only new things were a quilt and a thermos bottle.

title: Memories with my sister at Green Lake
content: Today I took a walk with Sister Yutong at Green Lake. We talked about how Dad used to take us to feed the black-headed gulls when we were little. It was hilarious the way she chased the gulls and fell. We also sat on the bench where I often come up with essay ideas (the third bench by the lake) and took photos.

title: Family walk materials.
content: Sister Sun Yutong talked about her first yoga experience and how funny the moves were. Dad recalled the first time he went to Qujing to see Grandma, and was so nervous that he held the gift upside down, but Grandma did not notice. Mom added that Grandma later secretly laughed at how clumsy he was. These details could be written as an essay.

title: Seeing her older sister off
content: Early this morning, the whole family went to Changshui Airport to see my sister off. Mom's eyes were slightly red when she hugged her, and Dad patted her on the shoulder and told her to report that she arrived safely. My sister urged me to keep writing well, saying that when she comes back for Spring Festival, she would check on my prose collection. I felt a little reluctant to see her go.

title: Reflections on a family walk at Green Lake.
content: Tonight I took a walk with my parents at Green Lake. Dad suddenly brought up the time he had opposed my sister going to Shenzhen, saying he was afraid she would suffer, but in the end he was moved by her determination and felt she had grown up. Mom then recalled sending packages to my sister every week, with hometown pickled vegetables, cured meat, and the flower cakes she loved — every week, without fail. I wrote down three words in my notebook: 'family, distance, support.' Looking at the many multi-generational families in the park, I suddenly understood even more — no matter how far apart, the hearts of family members are always connected.

title: Putting Up Spring Festival Couplets
content: I had planned to sort out my essay draft this morning, but my father asked me to put up Spring Festival couplets, so I had to put down my laptop. The whole family put up couplets together, and the atmosphere was lively.

title: New Year breakfast and family photo
content: I had planned to get up early and write something, but the whole family was in the dining room eating the tangyuan that Mom had made with sweet fermented rice wine, so I just joined them. My sister took a group photo with her Polaroid and stuck it on the fridge. A cozy morning.

title: Warm family dinner and reluctance to part.
content: Mom made sweet-and-sour squirrel fish and Yunnan-style stir-fry, Dad opened a bottle of red wine, and the whole family sat around chatting. Mentioning that my older sister is returning to Shenzhen tomorrow, everyone felt a bit reluctant to part; the atmosphere was warm but tinged with sadness.

title: A warm moment of family reunion
content: Helped Mom prepare vegetables in the living room; Dad watched the news and chimed in about cultural programs. We talked about the new coffee shop at the entrance to the neighborhood, and the atmosphere was very relaxed.

title: Gastrointestinal discomfort record
content: In the morning, she had a stomachache, so she went to Ziyuan Convenience Store and bought soda crackers and honey citron tea. After resting for fifteen minutes, she felt better.

title: Morning preparation notes
content: My legs were a bit sore, so after drinking warm water and eating two slices of bread, I took my stomach medicine with me, because I had to continue gathering material today.

title: Record of physical condition after completing the first draft.
content: I finally finished the first draft of Mother's Podium. My shoulders are terribly sore, and my stomach is a bit bloated. Three consecutive days of going out early and returning late for the used book drifting activity, plus rushing to finish the draft tonight, have taken a toll on my body. But I feel quite satisfied. I should be fine after some rest.

title: Shared the good news at a family lunch.
content: During lunch, I excitedly showed the screenshot of being shortlisted for the literary newcomer award. Mom happily put food in my bowl, while Dad reminded me not to get proud and told me to keep my voice steady in the afternoon interview.

title: Workshop Review - Core Theory of Characterization
content: In the afternoon: copied the core theories from the morning workshop with a black fountain pen and highlighted key quotes with a blue highlighter. Placed a sticky note beside the character creation chapter and completed a draft of a character biography.

title: Daily reflection notes.
content: Three key takeaways: details are the soul of a character; plot must follow the character's arc; you need a world in your heart. Completed a 10-minute gratitude meditation, thanking Editor Xu for the recognition, my mentor for the inspiration, and myself for being focused today.

title: Organizing workshop notes and working on the journal.
content: I saved the PPT screenshots and notes from the two-day workshop into Evernote by date, hand-drew a resonance formula chart, pasted in supermarket receipts and leaves, and completed the internalization of knowledge.

title: Workshop Day 3: editorial process and mentor feedback
content: Today I learned the editing process from source material to final draft, using feature story cases to explain how to select background material. I asked questions about the outline of my non-fiction story on the transformation of local old teahouses, and my mentor commented that 'the skeleton is not solid enough' and it needs clearer structural support.

title: One-on-one course feedback record
content: In the Q&A session at the end of today's class, I asked my advisor three questions: 1. How to strengthen the solidity of the story's skeleton? 2. What are the criteria for choosing details to include? 3. How to balance emotion and logic? My advisor looked at the shared screen with my two assignments, gave specific supplementary directions for the old teahouse outline, and commented that my writing 'has keen perception and a warm core, but the skeleton needs to be more solid.' I highlighted all the suggestions with a marker. I gained so much!

title: Workshop - Final Review
content: Saved the book list shared by classmates and the screenshots of the mentor's useful tips. Entered the mentor's targeted feedback on the two practice pieces, answers to questions, and the core formulas from the “Reader Interaction and Emotional Resonance” module.

title: Headstand breakthrough in yoga class
content: On my third attempt today, I finally succeeded in a headstand away from the wall. Core engaged, tailbone lifted, and I held it steadily for about 5 seconds! Coach He Lu said we can try a slow lift next class. I'm so happy.

title: Rainy morning run record at Green Lake Park.
content: Morning run of 5 km in the rain, pace 7:40 per kilometer, out-and-back from the east gate of Green Lake Park to the southeast corner.

title: Cross-Training Record by the Panlong River
content: 30 minutes of cross-training: 10 minutes of jogging to warm up, 5 sets of sprint-walking and slow-walking recovery intervals. As she listened to Chapter Five of 'Walden', the river breeze was cool and her body gradually warmed up.

title: A small breakthrough in the core and balance class.
content: Coach He Lu's core strengthening and balance class today was amazing! In the final inversion segment, I successfully tried a freestanding headstand and held it for about 7 seconds. The coach praised my progress. Keep up the good work!

title: Record of yoga in the guest room.
content: Today's 20-minute gentle yoga: Cat-Cow, Child's Pose, Downward-Facing Dog. The warm tropical breeze flowed in from the balcony, sweat dripped down my cheeks, and my body completely opened up. For the first time, I felt that sticking with exercise isn't that hard.

title: Evening yoga and foot-bathing record.
content: Sitting for a long time made my lower back sore. Tonight I did 30 minutes of yoga stretching and soaked my feet with lavender foot soak powder. My body feels much better. I need to keep exercising.

title: Reflections after a private rehabilitation yoga class.
content: Coach He's targeted abdominal breathing and Cat-Cow pose for the neck and shoulders were very effective; the shoulder soreness from long hours at a desk has clearly eased. Thank you for the free class.

title: Memo on finalizing the floral design plan.
content: Final plan: main flowers - white calla lilies + light green lisianthus, paired with areca palm and jasmine, using eco-friendly floral foam, budget 250 yuan. Shopping list: 10 stems of calla lilies, 5 stems of lisianthus, 3 areca palm fronds, 1 bunch of jasmine, 2 blocks of green floral foam. In preparation for scouting the flower market this afternoon.

title: Evening flower material sorting notes.
content: Tonight, arrange the flower materials: cut the dead branches diagonally and soak them in water; trim the gentian and smoketree leaves, wrap them in damp newspaper, and put them in the refrigerator to keep fresh; put the lisianthus in a glass vase on the desk.

title: Post-exam reflection and waiting.
content: The exam is over. The test topic was 'Autumn Sounds.' I made a slanted arrangement with dead branches, gentian, and smoke tree leaves. I think I did quite well, but waiting for the results makes me a little uneasy.

title: Mind-body balance check-in and neck-shoulder stretches.
content: Completed today: yoga class, walk, light dinner. The 10-minute shoulder and neck stretch before bed is done.

title: Summer light diet log
content: Today at lunch, my mother made tomato and egg noodles. They were light and delicious, fitting the summer diet plan.

title: Research plan for the three weeks before winter break.
content: Week 1: Closely read Yu Jian's Record of Kunming; Week 2: Closely read Lei Pingyang's essay collection and compare; Week 3: Look up theoretical materials and start writing the proposal.

title: Thoughts on 'Yunnan Dusk' and 'regional memory'.
content: After reading the literature, I gained a deeper understanding of the imagery of 'Yunnan Dusk,' but I'm confused about how to combine personal experience with an academic framework. In the 'regional memory' section, the materials seem to lean toward macro-narrative and lack micro-level individual perspectives. Should I supplement with oral history materials? Also, should the thesis proposal focus more on a specific location?

content: During an interview at Mingyuan Bookstore this afternoon, Uncle Qin said something memorable: "A bookstore is like a worm that hoards books, hiding itself in a corner of the city." That sentence struck me immediately. Maybe I can write an essay around this image.

title: Fuxian Lake self-driving route

content: Decided to adopt editor Xu's suggestions: 1. Delete 'Night Visit to the Finance University Old Book Stall', 'Old Times in the Bookstore', and 'One Afternoon'; 2. Adjust the choice of metaphors in 'An Afternoon at the Old Teahouse'. In the evening, I went for a walk in Green Lake Park to seek inspiration for the preface.

title: Key points for pronunciation correction practice
content: Pronunciation tips taught by my mother: for retroflex consonants, the tip of the tongue must touch the front of the hard palate; for distinguishing front and back nasal finals, the tip of the tongue touches the upper gums for front nasals, and the root of the tongue rises for back nasals. She also taught a "tongue-twisting" exercise: use the tip of the tongue to repeatedly press the inner sides of the upper and lower teeth for 5 minutes every day.
